claims.text: The exceptional dynamic strength–ductility balance in high-entropy alloys results from synergistic activation of deformation twinning and dislocation slip enabled by atomic-scale compositional heterogeneity.
CoCrFeNi or CoCrFeNiMn can be treated as a single-phase high-entropy alloy with inherent atomic-scale compositional fluctuations and a uniform microstructure.
Extended homogenization or alloying adjustments can minimize local compositional heterogeneity while leaving the overall phase and microstructure unchanged.
Chemical complexity and atomic-scale compositional heterogeneity produce spatially variable stacking-fault-energy landscapes.
Locally lower stacking fault energies favor deformation twinning, whereas locally higher stacking fault energies favor dislocation slip.
Spatially distributed, concurrent or sequential twinning and dislocation slip delay strain localization and necking.
The coordination of twinning and dislocation slip promotes uniform plastic deformation and high ductility at high flow stress.
Under dynamic loading, the native heterogeneous alloy will have greater uniform elongation than a homogenized variant.
The native heterogeneous alloy will have a higher density of twin–dislocation interactions than the homogenized variant.
The native heterogeneous alloy will retain high flow strength under tensile loading.
The native heterogeneous alloy will show higher strain hardening than the homogenized variant.
The native heterogeneous alloy will show more spatially distributed plasticity than the homogenized variant.
Reducing local stacking-fault-energy variation will reduce twinning activity.
The proposed mechanism should hold for single-phase FCC or FCC-based high-entropy alloys at room temperature under dynamic tensile loading.
Other phases or extreme temperatures may involve additional or different deformation mechanisms.
Room-temperature CoCrFeNi nanopillars exhibited uniform tensile elongation up to about 110% at a flow stress of 0.6–1.0 GPa.
Quantitative differences in twinning density and strain-hardening rate may depend on grain size, processing history, and testing conditions.
Comparable twinning activity, strain hardening, and uniform ductility in the reduced-heterogeneity control would falsify the proposed causal mechanism.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as the same alloy, but targeted alloying is offered as a way to create it. Targeted alloying changes composition and therefore would not constitute a strictly same-alloy control and could independently alter stacking-fault energy, phase stability, or deformation behavior.
